title: Event catalog & RBAC v2 interfacing — evidence automation notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Draft for a fourth iteration of the audit event catalog that ties RBAC v2 semantics into the schema and surfaces deterministic hooks for evidence automation + SIEM exports. This doc is intentionally informal — working notes for the security, infra, and SRE teams.

Scope:
- Canonical event fields for all user/service actions (API calls, console UI, system-authorized automation)
- RBAC v2 specific fields to capture effective permissions at time of event
- Evidence automation metadata (what to collect, URIs, hashes) and trigger points
- SIEM export mappings (JSONL, CEF, Splunk HEC) and compatibility guidance
- Versioning and migration strategy from current live schemas (v1..v3) to this draft (v4)

High-level goals:
- Make each event a self-describing record that can be used for policy investigations and automation replay
- Ensure minimal performance impact on serving runtime (bounded extra fields, optional enrichment pipeline)
- Provide deterministic fields for automated evidence collection and proof-of-action generation
- Keep backwards compatibility via schema_version and field aliases for older consumers

Schema highlights (canonical fields):
- schema_version: string (e.g., "audit.v4")  // top-level, used by parsers to route to the correct decoder
- event_id: uuid 
- timestamp: rfc3339
- actor_type: [user | service | api_key | system]
- actor_id: string  // user id, service principal id, key id
- actor_display_name: string (optional)
- actor_permissions_snapshot: string (compact base64 json)  -- snapshot of effective RBAC v2 policy for the actor at event time
- actor_roles: string (comma list) -- resolved roles for quick queries
- action: string (canonical verb e.g., read, write, start, stop, grant, revoke)
- resource_type: string (e.g., model, deployment, project, key, audit-config)
- resource_id: string
- resource_parent: string (optional)  // project or org id
- request_id: string  // correlates to client request / trace
- trace_id: string  // distributed tracing id
- outcome: [success | failure | partial]  // high-level outcome
- outcome_code: string (optional)  // e.g., error code, HTTP status
- attributes: string (compact json base64) // free-form event attributes for rich queries (size capped)
- diff_snapshot_ref: string (optional) // pointer to resource state diff stored in evidence store
- evidence_artifact_uri: string (S3/GCS/secure blob)  // automated evidence collector writes here
- evidence_hash: string (sha256 hex)  // integrity check for artifact
- evidence_collection_trigger: [on_write | on_error | periodic | manual]  // why evidence was captured
- pii_flags: string (comma list)  // low-cardinality tags for downstream redaction policies
- retention_label: string (e.g., legal-hold, standard, 90d)
- service_context: string (optional)  // runtime region/cluster/pool id
- schema_compat_aliases: string (optional) // if we had to map old fields during migration

RBAC v2-specific notes:
- actor_permissions_snapshot must contain: policy_version, allowed_actions (short list), role_bindings (id list), effective_role_ids. We intentionally store a compact snapshot so post-hoc access checks are reproducible without hitting the policy engine.
- Snapshot format: compact JSON -> base64 -> stored in actor_permissions_snapshot. Example unencoded: {"policy_version":"v2.3","allowed_actions":["deploy:create","model:load"],"roles":["infra-deployer"],"bindings":["rb-123"]}  // keep small (<2KB).
- When an event is caused by impersonation or 'run-as', populate actor_delegate_id and impersonation_chain (comma list) so auditors can reconstruct the chain.

Evidence automation hooks and minimal pipeline:
- Triggers: outcome=failure for high-risk actions (grant/revoke, key_create, private_deploy), periodic snapshots for deployments or on explicit retention_label=legal-hold
- Collector job writes artifacts to evidence bucket with path template: s3://redwood-evidence/{org}/{project}/{event_id}/{artifact-type}.{ext}
- Event includes evidence_artifact_uri + evidence_hash + automation_run_id so consumers can rehydrate evidence deterministically.
- Evidence types: request-body, full-response, rendered-console-snapshot, policy-evaluation-record, pre/post resource state diffs.
- Encryption: all evidence written via customer-specific KMS when appropriate (private deploys). Include kms_key_ref field in artifact metadata (not in event payload) — reference is stored in the evidence store UI.

SIEM export and consumer considerations:
- We will export a flattened subset to SIEMs: {timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_roles, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, outcome_code, request_id, trace_id, severity} where severity is mapped from outcome/action/risk label.
- Preferred export formats: 
  - JSONL (primary): one JSON per line, full events truncated to 16KB
  - CEF (secondary): map core fields to CEF header+extension for legacy SIEMs
  - Splunk HEC: bulk batched upload with compressed payloads (gzip)
- Field mapping doc (short):
  - event_id -> eventId
  - timestamp -> start
  - actor_id -> srcUser
  - resource_type/resource_id -> cs1Label=resource, cs1=resource_id
  - action -> operation
  - evidence_artifact_uri -> cs2
- PII/redaction: SIEM pipeline must apply redaction rules before forwarding. Redaction decisions are based on pii_flags and org-level policy. We will include a redaction_hash for replaced values so forensic reassembly is possible if authorized.

Versioning & migration plan (v1..v3 -> v4):
- schema_version is authoritative. Parsers should support tolerant decoding: unknown fields are ignored, missing optional fields are allowed.
- Migration steps:
  1) Introduce schema_version=audit.v4 alongside existing producers for 2 weeks; consumers log usage and errors.
  2) Flip producer flag to make actor_permissions_snapshot optional but recommended. Consumers warned via slack/jira.
  3) Enable evidence_artifact_uri on high-risk events only (can be toggled).
  4) After 6 weeks, default to including evidence hooks for all write actions.
  5) Deprecation: keep v1/v2 parsers for 6 months, maintain a compatibility shim in the enrichment pipeline that can synthesize missing actor_roles from older fields where possible.

Backwards compatibility guidance for downstream teams:
- If you consume audit events, prefer reading schema_version first. If unknown, route to the compatibility parser.
- Use new fields if present but fallback to older fields (we will publish an alias map). Examples of aliasing: actor -> actor_id, user -> actor_display_name.
- Avoid hard-failing on unknown attributes. Add feature flagging for strict-mode to help transition.

Examples (JSONL sample, trimmed):
{
  "schema_version": "audit.v4",
  "event_id": "8a3f9b12-1c2e-4d9b-9a2f-5b3e7a6c9d4f",
  "timestamp": "2024-11-19T15:22:33Z",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "actor_id": "user:ajpatel",
  "actor_roles": "admin,security-auditor",
  "actor_permissions_snapshot": "eyJwb2xpY3lfdmVyc2lvbiI6InYyLjMiLCJhbGxvd2VkX2FjdGlvbnMiOlsicmVtb3RlOnJlYWQiXX0=",
  "action": "grant:role",
  "resource_type": "project",
  "resource_id": "proj-42",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req-9911",
  "evidence_artifact_uri": "s3://redwood-evidence/acme/proj-42/8a3f9b12/console-snapshot.png",
  "evidence_hash": "d2d2f0...",
  "pii_flags": "none"
}

Open questions / TODOs (please add inline):
- How large can actor_permissions_snapshot be before it impacts ingestion throughput? target <2KB but need benchmarking. @Marco to run perf tests.
- Canonical list of high-risk actions for automatic evidence collection (initial proposal: grant, revoke, key_create, deployment_start, private_deploy). Need product confirmation. @Sam Lee to sync with product-hosted-api.
- Retention policy enforcement: who owns evidence store purge for private deployments (customer-managed) vs hosted? Legal/Support/Infra to align.
- Should we standardize evidence artifact naming across Hosted/Dedicated/Private? proposal: yes, with an org prefix.
- SIEM mapping: do we publish a versioned mapping table (recommended) or embed in the schema registry? leaning towards separate mapping table (confluence page) so SIEM teams can customize.

Rollout owner and next steps:
- Owner: Aisha Patel (security)
- Engineering lead for producer changes: Marco Diaz (platform infra)
- Evidence automation implementation: Samantha Lee (infra-eng)
- SIEM and GTM communication: Omar Khan (security eng)

Immediate next actions (7 days):
- Marco: perf budget tests for base64 snapshot sizes and ingestion throughput (due 2024-11-27)
- Sam: prototype collector that writes an evidence artifact for grant/revoke events (due 2024-11-29)
- Helen: draft Confluence export mapping table and Slack announcement (due 2024-11-25)

References / links:
- jira:SEC-4321 (schema change request)
- github:infra/audit-schema#78 (prototype code for v4 encoder)
- confluence:SEC-AUDIT-EVENTS (mapping tables + existing v1..v3 docs)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally iterative; comment inline in the doc or drop notes to #security-sig. We will lock to v4-beta for a 2-week canary window before making it the default for all producers.

End of draft.
